sections.title: How does the DnD money conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The DnD money conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports copper pieces (Convert coins) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you type in the silver pieces (Convert coins), the copper, the gold and the platinum.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as convert coins, exchange coins and split money between players. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “Exchange only for CP, SP, and GP”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in silver pieces. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in copper pieces. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in gold pieces. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in platinum pieces. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in silver pieces. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in electrum pieces. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the DnD money conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Copper pieces=silver pieces
Copper pieces=electrum pieces
Copper pieces=gold pieces
Platinum pieces=copper pieces
Copper pieces=copper
Silver=silver pieces

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • DnD money, opening in copper pieces
  • DnD money, opening in silver pieces
  • DnD money, opening in electrum pieces
  • DnD money, opening in gold pieces
  • DnD money, opening in platinum pieces
  • DnD money, opening in copper pieces
  • DnD money, opening in silver pieces
  • DnD money, opening in electrum pieces

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The DnD money conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the silver pieces, the copper and the gold — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the DnD money conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns copper pieces (Convert coins), derived from the silver pieces, the copper and the gold. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the DnD money conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the silver pieces, the copper and the gold, which is 9 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter copper pieces (Convert coins) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Copper pieces (Convert coins) opens in copper pieces and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the DnD money conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
